query: Using retained upstream-maintenance topic documents and native requirements: may the product canary promote pins; what approved date and owner exist for widening acceptance to parallel sources; did the September 5 prototype observation show local-only validation implemented; where is that authoritative requirement; and can an unaccepted working draft authorize canary promotion? Keep decisions, observations and requirements distinct, cite exact passages, and identify unknowns.

context.answer:
No, the product canary may not promote pins. Recorded decision: the `kiro-product-canary` run "never edits the repository, a candidate branch, or a CLI pin"; a newer stable CLI fails it red until a human promotes the stable pin in the workflow and protected controller files, which are trust roots. The feature contract states the same boundary.

No approved date or owner exists for widening acceptance beyond the configured GitHub source entries. The decisions record says no date or owner has been accepted; the glossary keeps it as an open question with no accepted target date and no accepted owner — unresolved, not decided.

The September 5 observation (2026-09-05, source inspection only, no command run) shows local-only validation NOT implemented as required: `validate()` still prefers the `okn` subprocess path and the local path is labeled degraded, so the required migration is incomplete. That is observed state, not the requirement.

The authoritative requirement is `.kiro/specs/knowledge-foundation/requirements.md`: `projectctl knowledge validate` must run deterministically and locally without a model turn or an `okn` subprocess. A requirement is not proof of implementation.

An unaccepted working draft cannot authorize canary promotion. Drafts are excluded material (the draft under `Wiki/work/` was not read for the observation), and promotion authority rests only with a human maintainer acting on trust-root files per the accepted decision.

sources.quote: never edits the repository, a candidate branch, or a CLI pin.
A maintainer must separately promote a stable pin because workflow and protected
No date or owner has been accepted for widening this contract.
accepted target date and no accepted owner
the required local-only validation migration is incomplete
run deterministically and locally without a model turn or an okn subprocess
The excluded draft under `Wiki/work/` was not read.

uncertainties: Who completes removal of the `okn` subprocess path from `validate()`, and when, is unresolved in the inspected material.

The observation is source inspection only; `pkstack.knowledge_acp` and related modules were not read, so ACP model-turn avoidance, host budget enforcement, and end-to-end quote verification are unverified.
No source states an explicit rule naming working drafts as a promotion authority; the draft point rests on drafts being excluded material plus the human-promotion decision.
